items.subject: physical-education-aqa
items.title: Muscles and Antagonistic Pairs
items.reason: The video associates pushing down into a press-up with elbow extension and the triceps acting as agonist, which contradicts the biomechanics examined at GCSE (the downward phase is elbow flexion) and will lose students marks on movement analysis questions.

mark_affecting.quote: The moment you push down into a press up, boom, those roles completely reverse.

items.subject: physical-education-aqa
items.title: Synovial Joints and Types of Movement
items.reason: The video swaps the textbook sporting examples of rotation and circumduction, teaching students that cricket bowling is rotation rather than circumduction, which is a spec-defined question on GCSE PE exams.

mark_affecting.quote: Picture a cricket bowler's arm rotating at the shoulder during a delivery. Circumduction is slightly different... kind of like when a javelin thrower really winds up.

items.subject: physical-education-aqa
items.title: Health, Fitness and the Components of Fitness
items.reason: The video states that a 100m sprinter requires muscular endurance in the final 20m, which contradicts the GCSE specification definition of muscular endurance (prolonged repeated contractions) and would lose marks on an exam question evaluating sprinting fitness components.

mark_affecting.quote: And in the final 20m, they desperately need muscular endurance to sustain that near-maximal effort and fight off that burning accumulation of lactic acid

items.title: Earth-Moon-Sun: Scale, Eclipses and Tides
items.reason: The video incorrectly states that total solar eclipses occur 'a few per decade for any specific location on Earth' instead of roughly once every 400 years, which would lose marks on questions concerning eclipse frequency and rarity.

mark_affecting.quote: total solar eclipses are super rare, restricted to just a few per decade for any specific location on Earth.
